candidateReviews.label: Confirmation bias

candidateReviews.label: Special pleading
candidateReviews.context: The Miracles that take place are consistent with the message of the New Testament itself
candidateReviews.rationale: Internal agreement with the New Testament message is offered as favorable testing without an equivalent independent standard for rival traditions.

candidateReviews.label: Ambiguity effect
candidateReviews.context: historians can only trace and weigh human activities and events
candidateReviews.rationale: Price explains a disciplinary limit on tracing causes, not a preference for familiar claims merely because uncertainty makes alternatives uncomfortable.

candidateReviews.label: Equivocation
candidateReviews.context: the only way you can Define truth is by its internal consistency
candidateReviews.rationale: The standard is inadequate because coherence does not guarantee truth, but White does not shift one term between distinct meanings.

candidateReviews.label: Ambiguity effect
candidateReviews.context: the further back you go everything has to be held open
candidateReviews.rationale: Price calibrates confidence to evidential scarcity and expressly remains open, rather than rejecting ancient claims simply because they are uncertain.

candidateReviews.label: Special pleading
candidateReviews.context: there is no parallel between the two because we do not have anything from that first century
candidateReviews.rationale: White supplies a principled temporal distinction between the traditions, even though he still owes fuller comparative evidence about transmission controls.

candidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance
candidateReviews.context: someone's idea of what the apostles would have done is mere speculation
candidateReviews.rationale: Price challenges an unsupported guarantee and does not infer that contamination occurred solely because complete apostolic policing has not been proven.

candidateReviews.label: Red herring

candidateReviews.rationale: White redirects the dispute to one conventional phrase while leaving Price’s broader claimed narrative sequence and motifs substantially unanswered.

candidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance

candidateReviews.label: Confirmation bias

candidateReviews.rationale: Price favors interpolation from compressed tensions while dismissing contextual reconciliation without testing the competing readings passage by passage.

candidateReviews.label: Belief bias

candidateReviews.rationale: White treats the absence of a passage-free witness as proof of originality without establishing that recoverable manuscript branches predate a possible insertion.

candidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance
candidateReviews.context: there is no evidence whatsoever and all sorts of evidence against any standardization
candidateReviews.rationale: White primarily cites positive early textual diversity against centralized standardization rather than relying only on failure to prove such an event.

candidateReviews.label: Confirmation bias
candidateReviews.context: it is filled with internal indications that it is late material
candidateReviews.rationale: Price’s interpretation is underdetermined, but he identifies concrete structure and function rather than merely selecting evidence because the conclusion is congenial.

candidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance
candidateReviews.context: how could streams reflecting the older text be completely lost to history
candidateReviews.rationale: White presses a legitimate evidential burden as a question and does not here claim that missing contrary witnesses conclusively prove originality.

candidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance
candidateReviews.context: there is no reason to think this is a post-crucifixion concept
candidateReviews.rationale: White gives the saying a concrete contemporary meaning, so his case rests on positive intelligibility rather than solely on absent disproof.

candidateReviews.label: Confirmation bias
candidateReviews.context: people are quick to misinterpret what they hear filtering it through expectations and biases
candidateReviews.rationale: Price proposes expectation-driven variation, but the cited textual differences alone do not show that he selectively discounted known contrary evidence.

candidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance
candidateReviews.context: how do you know they were not quoting Jesus when much talking is unrecorded
candidateReviews.rationale: White uses unrecorded discussion to block Price’s inference from silence, not to assert that Jesus was quoted because absence cannot be disproved.

candidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance
candidateReviews.context: no one mentions Jesus saying anything and if he had these debates would never have happened
candidateReviews.rationale: Price makes Acts’ failure to report a quotation prove that no remembered instruction existed, despite acknowledging selective reporting and alternative sequencing.

candidateReviews.label: Subjective validation
candidateReviews.context: the consistency that I find in Scripture is tremendously different from the Apollonius story
candidateReviews.rationale: White treats his personally perceived coherence as comparative support while supplying no paired examples or independent measure that listeners can verify.

candidateReviews.label: Red herring
candidateReviews.context: a later passage can still be profound no matter who said it
candidateReviews.rationale: The point distinguishes value from provenance and remains relevant to inspiration, even though it does not independently decide historical reliability.

candidateReviews.label: Subjective validation
candidateReviews.context: there is a beauty to the harmony of God's word that absolutely amazes me
candidateReviews.rationale: White explicitly offers personal amazement and perceived harmony as support for divine unity without independent tests separating it from harmonizing interpretation.

candidateReviews.label: Confirmation bias
candidateReviews.context: inspiration hindered understanding by walling off things that cannot mean error
candidateReviews.rationale: Price criticizes a prior interpretive constraint and requests openness to alternatives; this does not itself exhibit his selective treatment of contrary evidence.

overallBlunderCandidateReviews.label: Equivocation
overallBlunderCandidateReviews.context: the only way you can define truth is by its internal consistency
overallBlunderCandidateReviews.rationale: White overstates coherence as a truth test, but he uses consistency steadily rather than changing a key word’s meaning midargument.

overallBlunderCandidateReviews.label: Subjective validation
overallBlunderCandidateReviews.context: I find fundamental differences and tremendous consistency in Scripture compared with Apollonius
overallBlunderCandidateReviews.rationale: The claimed comparative superiority rests on White’s reported impression without paired evidence enabling the audience to assess the difference independently.

overallBlunderCandidateReviews.label: Belief bias
overallBlunderCandidateReviews.context: the conversion of Paul just screams literary origin because the sources are amazingly similar
overallBlunderCandidateReviews.rationale: Price’s intuitive sense of obvious literary origin replaces the detailed correspondences required for the conclusion to follow from his comparison.

overallBlunderCandidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance
overallBlunderCandidateReviews.context: Justin Martyr never mentions Paul and known Paulinist Christians appear only with later groups
overallBlunderCandidateReviews.rationale: The reconstruction turns gaps in surviving references into support for a contested late identity theory without an independently dated evidential chain.
